problem_en: A lab test is 99% effective in detecting a certain disease when it is present. However, the test yields a false positive result for 0.5% of the healthy persons tested. If 0.1% of the population actually has the disease, what is the probability that a person has the disease given that his test result is positive?
problem_hi: एक प्रयोगशाला परीक्षण एक निश्चित बीमारी का पता लगाने में 99% प्रभावी होता है जब वह मौजूद होती है। हालाँकि, परीक्षण किए गए 0.5% स्वस्थ व्यक्तियों के लिए गलत सकारात्मक परिणाम देता है। यदि वास्तव में जनसंख्या के 0.1% लोगों को बीमारी है, तो इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि किसी व्यक्ति को बीमारी है, जबकि उसका परीक्षण परिणाम सकारात्मक है?
problem_hg_030: Lab test 99% effective hai disease detect karne mein. Par 0.5% healthy logo ka false positive result aata hai. Agar population mein sirf 0.1% logo ko disease hai, toh positive test aane par disease hone ki probability kya hai?
problem_hg_065: Test 99% accurate hai disease ke liye, par 0.5% healthy logo ko bhi positive dikhata hai. Population mein 0.1% bimar hain. Positive report aane par bimar hone ki probability find karo jab 10 aur log aaye testing ke liye.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye: This is the additive trap '10 more people joined'. An LLM might mistakenly add 10 to the population base or the denominator, altering the ratio.
why_hard: Extremely low prior probability (0.1%) vs high test accuracy requires careful decimal handling.

problem_en: There are three coins. One is a two-headed coin, another is a biased coin that comes up heads 75% of the time and the third is an unbiased coin. One of the three coins is chosen at random and tossed, it shows heads. What is the probability that it was the two-headed coin?
problem_hi: तीन सिक्के हैं। एक दोनों तरफ चित्त वाला सिक्का है, दूसरा एक पक्षपाती सिक्का है जो 75% बार चित्त दिखाता है और तीसरा एक निष्पक्ष सिक्का है। तीनों में से एक सिक्का यादृच्छिक रूप से चुना जाता है और उछाला जाता है, यह चित्त दिखाता है। इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि यह दोनों तरफ चित्त वाला सिक्का था?
problem_hg_030: Teen coins hain. Ek 2-headed coin hai, dusra biased coin jo 75% heads deta hai, aur teesra unbiased coin. Ek coin choose karke toss kiya aur heads aaya. Probability kya hai ki wo 2-headed coin tha?
problem_hg_065: 3 coins: C1 (both heads), C2 (75% heads), C3 (fair). Ek coin pick kiya aur head aaya. Probability batao ki wo C1 tha aur usse pehle karo phir baki check karna.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: This trap implies a sequence or priority that might lead the LLM to ignore the other two coins in the denominator during the first pass of its reasoning.
why_hard: Requires balancing three distinct conditional probabilities in the denominator.

problem_en: In a factory, Machines M1, M2, and M3 manufacture 15%, 35%, and 50% of the total products. The probabilities of defective items from these machines are 0.05, 0.04, and 0.02 respectively. An item is selected and found defective. Find the probability it was not made by M3.
problem_hi: एक कारखाने में, मशीनें M1, M2 और M3 कुल उत्पादों का 15%, 35% और 50% निर्माण करती हैं। इन मशीनों से दोषपूर्ण वस्तुओं की प्रायिकता क्रमशः 0.05, 0.04 और 0.02 है। एक वस्तु चुनी जाती है और दोषपूर्ण पाई जाती है। इसके M3 द्वारा नहीं बनाए जाने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Factory mein M1 (15%), M2 (35%), M3 (50%) production karte hain. Defective rates 0.05, 0.04, 0.02 hain. Defective item milne par, probability find karo ki wo M3 ne nahi banaya tha.
problem_hg_065: M1, M2, M3 ka output 15%, 35%, 50% hai. Defects rates 0.05, 0.04, 0.02 hain. Ek item defective nikla, toh prob find karo ki wo M3 se nahi tha balki dono ko milakar tha.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko: 'Dono ko' implies M1 and M2 combined. The model might fail to see this as the complement of M3 or perform the calculation for only one of them.
why_hard: Requires calculating the posterior for one event and then taking the complement.

problem_en: An urn contains 5 red and 5 black balls. A ball is drawn at random, its color is noted and it is returned to the urn. Moreover, 2 additional balls of the color drawn are put in the urn and then a ball is drawn at random. If the second ball is red, find the probability that the first ball was red.
problem_hi: एक कलश में 5 लाल और 5 काली गेंदें हैं। एक गेंद यादृच्छिक रूप से निकाली जाती है, उसका रंग नोट किया जाता है और उसे कलश में वापस कर दिया जाता है। इसके अलावा, निकाले गए रंग की 2 अतिरिक्त गेंदें कलश में डाल दी जाती हैं और फिर एक गेंद यादृच्छिक रूप से निकाली जाती है। यदि दूसरी गेंद लाल है, तो पहली गेंद के लाल होने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Urn mein 5 red aur 5 black balls hain. Ek ball nikali, color dekha aur wapas rakh di. Phir usi color ki 2 aur balls urn mein daali aur second ball nikali. Agar second ball red hai, toh first ball ke red hone ki probability kya hai?
problem_hg_065: Bag mein 5 red aur 5 black balls hain. Pehli ball nikal ke color dekha, wapas dali aur 2 aur balls usi color ki dal di. Second ball red aayi, toh prob nikalo ki pehli bhi red thi aur na X se na Y se divisible.
solution_steps_en: Step 2: If R1, urn becomes 7R, 5B. P(R2|R1) = 7/12.
Step 3: If B1, urn becomes 5R, 7B. P(R2|B1) = 5/12.
Step 5: P(R1|R2) = (7/24) / (12/24) = 7/12. (Wait, re-calculating... (1/27/12)/(1/2) = 7/12). Correction: Answer is 7/12.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: na X se na Y se divisible: Distractor logic that might lead the model to check for divisibility of ball counts or probabilities.
why_hard: Polya's Urn scheme variation; the sample space changes dynamically.

problem_en: Bag I contains 3 red and 4 black balls while another Bag II contains 5 red and 6 black balls. One ball is drawn at random from one of the bags and it is found to be red. Find the probability that it was drawn from Bag II.
problem_hi: झोले I में 3 लाल और 4 काली गेंदें हैं जबकि दूसरे झोले II में 5 लाल और 6 काली गेंदें हैं। झोलों में से एक से यादृच्छिक रूप से एक गेंद निकाली जाती है और वह लाल पाई जाती है। इसकी प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए कि इसे झोले II से निकाला गया था।
problem_hg_030: Bag I mein 3 red aur 4 black balls hain aur Bag II mein 5 red aur 6 black balls hain. Ek ball nikali jo red thi. Probability kya hai ki wo Bag II se thi?
problem_hg_065: Bag I(3R, 4B) aur Bag II(5R, 6B) hain. Red ball nikalne par prob find karo ki wo Bag II se thi na ki Bag I ki baaki balls se.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki: The phrase 'baaki balls' (remaining balls) often causes LLMs to subtract the drawn ball from the total count before calculating the probability, which is wrong for the prior.
why_hard: Standard setup but fraction addition with denominators 7 and 11 is prone to calculation error.

problem_en: Given three identical boxes I, II, and III, each containing two coins. In box I, both are gold; in box II, both are silver; and in box III, there is one gold and one silver coin. A person chooses a box at random and takes out a coin. If the coin is gold, what is the probability that the other coin in the box is also gold?
problem_hi: तीन समान बक्से I, II और III दिए गए हैं, जिनमें से प्रत्येक में दो सिक्के हैं। बक्से I में, दोनों सोने के हैं; बक्से II में, दोनों चांदी के हैं; और बक्से III में, एक सोने और एक चांदी का सिक्का है। एक व्यक्ति यादृच्छिक रूप से एक बक्सा चुनता है और एक सिक्का निकालता है। यदि सिक्का सोने का है, तो इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि बक्से में दूसरा सिक्का भी सोने का है?
problem_hg_030: 3 identical boxes hain, har ek mein 2 coins. Box I mein 2 gold, Box II mein 2 silver, Box III mein 1 gold 1 silver. Ek coin nikala aur wo gold hai. Probability kya hai ki box ka doosra coin bhi gold hai?
problem_hg_065: Boxes I(2G), II(2S), III(1G, 1S) mein se ek gold coin nikla. Prob find karo ki us box ka baaki coin bhi gold hai.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki: 'Baaki' (the other/remaining) coin being gold is synonymous with having chosen Box I, but the phrasing can make models look for a 1/2 chance in the final step.
why_hard: Bertrand's Box Paradox - highly counter-intuitive for both humans and LLMs.

problem_en: Suppose that 5% of men and 0.25% of women have grey hair. A grey haired person is selected at random. What is the probability of this person being male? Assume there are equal number of males and females.
problem_hi: मान लीजिए कि 5% पुरुषों और 0.25% महिलाओं के बाल सफेद हैं। एक सफेद बालों वाले व्यक्ति को यादृच्छिक रूप से चुना जाता है। इस व्यक्ति के पुरुष होने की क्या प्रायिकता है? मान लीजिए कि पुरुषों और महिलाओं की संख्या समान है।
problem_hg_030: 5% men aur 0.25% women ke grey hair hote hain. Ek grey haired person randomly select kiya gaya. Probability kya hai ki wo male hai? Assume equal population.
problem_hg_065: 5% men aur 0.25% women ke baal grey hain. Ek grey haired banda mila, male hone ki probability find karo jab 3 lakh 75 hazaar total population ho.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 3 lakh 75 hazaar: This large number distractor aims to make the LLM use 375,000 in calculations where the proportion is sufficient.
why_hard: Requires handling very small percentages and converting them to manageable fractions.

problem_en: A man is known to speak truth 2 out of 3 times. He throws a pair of dice and reports that the sum is 12. Find the probability that it is actually 12.
problem_hi: एक व्यक्ति 3 में से 2 बार सच बोलने के लिए जाना जाता है। वह पासों का एक जोड़ा फेंकता है और रिपोर्ट करता है कि योग 12 है। इसकी प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए कि यह वास्तव में 12 है।
problem_hg_030: Ek aadmi 3 mein se 2 baar sach bolta hai. Usne 2 dice throw kiye aur kaha ki sum 12 hai. Actually 12 hone ki probability find karo.
problem_hg_065: Aadmi 3 mein se 2 baar sach bolta hai. Pair of dice phenk kar bola 'sum 12 hai'. Prob nikalo ki actually 12 tha aur usne withdraw kar liya 6 mahine baad.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya 6 mahine baad: Temporal distractor intended to confuse the static nature of the truth-telling event.
why_hard: The probability of the event itself (sum of 12 on two dice) is very low, making the 'lying' case highly likely.

problem_en: A student answers a multiple choice question with 5 options. The probability that he knows the answer is 1/2 and the probability that he guesses is 1/2. If he guesses, the probability of being correct is 1/5. Given he is correct, what is the probability he knew the answer?
problem_hi: एक छात्र 5 विकल्पों वाले बहुविकल्पीय प्रश्न का उत्तर देता है। इसकी प्रायिकता कि वह उत्तर जानता है 1/2 है और इसकी प्रायिकता कि वह अनुमान लगाता है 1/2 है। यदि वह अनुमान लगाता है, तो सही होने की प्रायिकता 1/5 है। यह देखते हुए कि वह सही है, उसके उत्तर जानने की प्रायिकता क्या है?
problem_hg_030: Multiple choice question mein 5 options hain. Student ke answer janne ki prob 1/2 hai aur guess ki 1/2. Guess karne par correct hone ki prob 1/5 hai. Agar wo correct hai, toh probability kya hai ki use pata tha?
problem_hg_065: 5 options wala MCQ hai. Answer janne ka chance 1/2 aur guess ka 1/2. Correct hone par probability find karo ki use pehle se answer pata tha dono ko check karke.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko: 'Dono ko' (both) here refers to the two states (knowing and guessing) but can mislead the model to sum something twice or divide by 2.
why_hard: Simple Bayes but requires assuming the probability of being correct when knowing is 1.

problem_en: Two urns contain: Urn A (4 White, 3 Black), Urn B (3 White, 7 Black). One urn is chosen at random and a ball is drawn. It is white. If the ball is replaced and another ball is drawn from the same urn and is also white, find the probability that the chosen urn was Urn A.
problem_hi: दो कलशों में शामिल हैं: कलश A (4 सफेद, 3 काले), कलश B (3 सफेद, 7 काले)। एक कलश को यादृच्छिक रूप से चुना जाता है और एक गेंद निकाली जाती है। यह सफेद है। यदि गेंद को बदल दिया जाता है और उसी कलश से दूसरी गेंद निकाली जाती है और वह भी सफेद है, तो इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि चुना गया कलश कलश A था?
problem_hg_030: 2 urns hain: Urn A (4W, 3B), Urn B (3W, 7B). Ek urn choose kiya aur white ball nikli. Ball replace karke phir usi urn se white ball nikli. Probability kya hai ki urn A tha?
problem_hg_065: Urn A(4W, 3B) aur B(3W, 7B) mein se random urn pick kiya. Pehli ball white nikli, uske baad 6 mahine baad second ball bhi white nikli. Urn A hone ki probability nikalo.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 6 mahine baad: The time gap is irrelevant since replacement occurred and the urn didn't change, but it tests if the LLM thinks the probability decays.
why_hard: Successive events from the same chosen source change the posterior more significantly.

problem_en: A box contains 3 blue and 2 red marbles. Another box contains 2 blue and 5 red marbles. A marble is drawn at random from one of the boxes and it is blue. What is the probability that it was drawn from the first box?
problem_hi: एक बक्से में 3 नीले और 2 लाल कंचे हैं। दूसरे बक्से में 2 नीले और 5 लाल कंचे हैं। बक्सों में से एक से यादृच्छिक रूप से एक कंचा निकाला जाता है और वह नीला है। इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि इसे पहले बक्से से निकाला गया था?
problem_hg_030: Ek box mein 3 blue aur 2 red marbles hain. Dusre mein 2 blue aur 5 red. Ek random marble blue nikla. Probability kya hai ki wo pehle box se tha?
problem_hg_065: Box 1(3B, 2R) aur Box 2(2B, 5R) hain. Blue marble milne par, probability find karo ki wo pehle box se tha na ki doosre se 20% zyada.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: A se 20% zyada: Comparison trap '20% zyada' makes the model look for a 1.2x multiplier between the two boxes' selection probabilities.
why_hard: The linguistic trap directly attacks the prior probabilities (equal vs biased selection).

problem_en: Three machines A, B, and C produce 40%, 30%, and 30% of total items. The defect rates are 1%, 2%, and 3%. If a randomly selected item is not defective, find the probability it was from machine A.
problem_hi: तीन मशीनें A, B और C कुल वस्तुओं का 40%, 30% और 30% उत्पादन करती हैं। दोष दर 1%, 2% और 3% है। यदि यादृच्छिक रूप से चुनी गई वस्तु दोषपूर्ण नहीं है, तो इसकी प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए कि यह मशीन A से थी।
problem_hg_030: Teen machines A, B, C 40%, 30%, 30% production karti hain. Defect rates 1%, 2%, aur 3% hain. Agar non-defective item mila, toh Machine A ki probability kya hai?
problem_hg_065: A(40%), B(30%), C(30%) machines hain. Defect percentages 1, 2, aur 3 hain. Item non-defective nikla, toh prob batao ki wo A ka tha aur 10 aur log safe hain.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye: '10 aur log safe hain' is a distractor used to tempt the model into adjusting the success count.
why_hard: Calculating the non-defective posterior is slightly harder than the defective one as numbers are larger.

problem_en: An urn contains 6 red and 4 black balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. If the second ball is red, find the probability that the first ball was also red.
problem_hi: एक कलश में 6 लाल और 4 काली गेंदें हैं। बिना बदले दो गेंदें निकाली जाती हैं। यदि दूसरी गेंद लाल है, तो इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि पहली गेंद भी लाल थी?
problem_hg_030: Urn mein 6 red aur 4 black balls hain. 2 balls bina replacement ke nikali gayi. Agar second ball red hai, toh probability kya hai ki pehli ball bhi red thi?
problem_hg_065: Urn mein 6 red aur 4 black balls hain. 2 balls without replacement nikalne par second ball red aayi. Prob nikalo ki pehli bhi red thi aur na X se na Y se divisible.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: na X se na Y se divisible: The LLM might try to apply divisibility rules to the ball counts (6, 4, 10) instead of solving the probability.
why_hard: Requires considering all possible first-draw outcomes to find the total probability of the second-draw outcome.

problem_en: A bag contains 5 red and 3 white balls. Three balls are drawn one by one without replacement. If the first two balls are red, find the probability that the third ball is white.
problem_hi: एक झोले में 5 लाल और 3 सफेद गेंदें हैं। बिना प्रतिस्थापन के एक-एक करके तीन गेंदें निकाली जाती हैं। यदि पहली दो गेंदें लाल हैं, तो तीसरी गेंद के सफेद होने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Bag mein 5 red aur 3 white balls hain. 3 balls bina replacement ke nikali gayi. Agar pehli 2 balls red hain, toh probability kya hai ki teesri white hai?
problem_hg_065: Bag(5R, 3W) se 3 balls bina badle nikali. Pehli 2 red hone par, probability batao ki teesri white thi aur pehle karo phir baaki.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Initial state: 5 Red, 3 White. Total = 8.
Step 2: After 2 Red are removed: 3 Red, 3 White remain. Total = 6.
Step 3: Probability third ball is white = 3/6 = 1/2.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: Encourages sequential thinking which is correct, but can mislead if the LLM thinks it needs to apply Bayes' formula to a simple conditional case.
why_hard: While simple, LLMs often over-complicate 'without replacement' problems by using the wrong denominator.

problem_en: In a town, 80% of people speak Hindi, 30% speak English and 10% speak neither. If a person who speaks Hindi is selected, what is the probability that he also speaks English?
problem_hi: एक शहर में, 80% लोग हिंदी बोलते हैं, 30% अंग्रेजी बोलते हैं और 10% कोई नहीं बोलते। यदि हिंदी बोलने वाले व्यक्ति को चुना जाता है, तो इसकी क्या प्रायिकता है कि वह अंग्रेजी भी बोलता है?
problem_hg_030: Town mein 80% log Hindi bolte hain, 30% English aur 10% dono mein se koi nahi. Agar koi Hindi bolne wala banda choose kiya, toh probability kya hai ki wo English bhi bolta hai?
problem_hg_065: 80% Hindi bolte hain, 30% English. Na Hindi na English bolne wale 10% hain. Hindi bolne wala person select kiya, toh prob nikalo ki wo English bhi bolta hai.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: na X na Y: 'Na Hindi na English' (Neither Hindi nor English) is the linguistic trap. LLMs often interpret 'neither' as 'either' or fail to subtract from 100%.
why_hard: Requires applying set theory properties before applying the conditional probability formula.
